title: OIDC callback can parse unbounded multipart bodies and leave temporary files
summary: An unauthenticated client can send multipart data to the GET-only OIDC callback. The OIDC parser spools multipart file parts to temporary storage before rejecting invalid state, and parsing request copies prevents ordinary request cleanup from removing the files. Requires OIDC configuration; a valid state cookie can be obtained by starting login without an account. Callback remains reachable with require-auth, read-only mode, and uploads disabled; upload size limits do not constrain it.
ai_role: The Yopass maintainer's case-specific security advisory explicitly credits Anthropic's OSS Scanner as discoverer (tracking identifier ANT-2026-WKMLNL5Z). It does not name a model version or internal discovery date.
classification_note: The public maintainer advisory documents the finding; it does not establish whether defenders knew of it or whether it was exploited before disclosure.
remediation_note: Yopass 16.0.0 fixes the issue (commit 0e393f62dc0f7550bfe7d0b7deb50575039a0a87). Affected-version scope: OIDC releases 14.0.0 through 15.1.0; fixed in 16.0.0 by passing http.NoBody to the GET callback parser while retaining query processing. Existing orphaned temp files are not removed by the code fix. Patch availability does not establish downstream deployment.

impacts.conditions: Repeated requests can grow temporary-disk and temporary-memory usage; the advisory says there is no traffic amplification and claims no secret disclosure.
impacts.exploitation: The advisory describes a possible or reproducible trigger as stated; it does not report observed exploitation in the wild.
